permitted_concomitant: topical moisturizers/emollients, bath oils, oatmeal bath preparations as needed

value.population_note: This is a psoriasis biologic active-comparator trial (bimekizumab vs. secukinumab), not an AD/TCS-flavored design, so regimen_type does not map to any of the 3 enum values (limited topical corticosteroid use on face/axilla/genitalia is explicitly permitted during the double-blind period, and expands to any topical steroid/vitamin D analog in the open-label extension). Left null as a real schema-enum gap; the permitted/prohibited concomitant lists below are the actual protocol Section 7.8 policy. Note the permitted topical policy differs by period: restricted to face/axilla/genitalia mild/low-potency steroids during the double-blind Treatment Period, but broadened to any topical steroid + vitamin D analog ointment during the OLE/OLE2 periods.

background_therapy.source_excerpt: Section 7.8.1.1 Topical medications: "In the double-blind Treatment Period, mild and low potency topical steroids will be permitted for use limited to the face, axilla, and/or genitalia, as needed... In the OLE and OLE2 Periods, the medications listed as permitted for the double-blind Treatment Period will be allowed. In addition, any topical steroids and vitamin D analog ointment will be permitted for use, as needed." Section 7.8.2, Table 7-4 Prohibited psoriasis medications: lists topicals (except permitted), systemic retinoids, systemic immunosuppressants, fumaric acid esters, systemic corticosteroids, phototherapy, anti-TNFs, ustekinumab, apremilast/tofacitinib, alefacept/efalizumab/guselkumab, tildrakizumab/risankizumab/briakinumab, and rituximab, each with a stated washout period.

co_primary_endpoints.label: PASI100 response at Week 16 (non-inferiority then superiority vs secukinumab)

multiplicity_control.source_excerpt: SAP Section 4.5 Multiple comparisons/multiplicity: "The statistical analysis of the primary efficacy variable and selected secondary efficacy variables will account for multiplicity and control the familywise Type I error rate at a 2-sided alpha level of 0.05 by using a fixed sequence testing procedure. The hypotheses (H1, H2, H3, H4, H5, and H6) comparing bimekizumab vs secukinumab will be tested at a 2-sided alpha level of 0.05. The first 2 hypotheses (H1 and H2) test whether bimekizumab is non-inferior and superior, respectively, to secukinumab for PASI100 response at Week 16. These are the hypothesis tests corresponding to the primary endpoint."

study_schedule.source_excerpt: Section 5.2 Study periods: "A Screening Period (2 to 5 weeks); A double-blind Treatment Period (48 weeks; final dose at Week 44); An optional OLE Period (96 weeks; final dose at Week 136 for subjects receiving bimekizumab 320mg Q8W and at Week 140 for subjects receiving bimekizumab 320mg Q4W) followed by a SFU Period (20 weeks after the final dose of IMP...)". Section 5.3: "For each subject, the study will last a maximum of up to 165 weeks."
